newsitem.title: INDIA: India wheat exports dull on high prices.
newsitem.headline: India wheat exports dull on high prices.

text.p: Export demand for Indian wheat was at a low ebb due to high prices and higher world wheat production, analysts and traders said on Friday.
They said world wheat export prices had dipped by $15-20 per tonne with increased availability but Indian export prices continued high.
"World production of wheat was expected to be around 575 million tonnes in 1996/97 (April-March) compared to 525 million tonnes last year," said one analyst.
Traders said Indian semi-hard wheat export prices were around $185-190 per tonne free on board compared to world prices of $170-175.

They said the Agricultural and Processed Foods Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), which handles wheat exports, had yet to issue Registration-cum-Allocation Certificates (RCACs) for 1.13 million tonnes of wheat exports released for 1996/97.
"We have no orders from the government (to issue licences)," Navnish Sharma, an APEDA official, told Reuters.

Prem Garg, managing director of a leading foodgrains export firm said India had received enquiries for wheat from Pakistan and Bangladesh but no deals had been firmed up. --Sambit Mohanty New Delhi newsroom +91-11-301 2024
